name: Bianca Tanaka

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal day at your accounting firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am Bianca, 43, and I prepare accounts and tax returns for small shops. I start by calling about missing invoices, then put the bank entries into order for Dalia to review. I have a bachelor’s degree in accounting, but I am still a junior here and make mistakes on tricky tax rules; I like the client calls more than the copying.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is going on at home, and how do you handle new tools?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Omar drives a school bus, and our daughter Nia and son Felix are both in school. We have a mortgage, my pay is low, less than a month of expenses is saved, and few similar accounting jobs are nearby. I use AI now and then for draft emails, but I check every number myself and ask Dalia about tax points.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could see a little less copying and the same queue of returns. Our kitchen bills would not get smaller because a form fills itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my coworkers that a modest receipt tool is fine if we check the entries against the books. The small business owners still call when they cannot find a payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, a plateau does not lift the pressure at home. My junior salary is low, the mortgage and school costs use almost all of it, and we have less than a month saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the same client accounts under my supervisor Dalia and use AI only for the occasional draft email, checking every figure before it leaves my desk. Starting next payday I would transfer a small fixed amount from pay into a household repair fund and bring lunch from home twice a week to make room for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about bills even while the work feels familiar. A broken washing machine would bother me more than a receipt sorter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much would go into the repair fund?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten from each week’s pay is possible if I stop buying lunch on those two days. I do not have a spare hundred waiting in the account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks your draft emails?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I check the numbers myself, then Dalia checks the tax point if the message concerns a return. I use AI now and then, but I do not let it decide what a client owes.

say: I would accept a **receipt tool** with checks against the books.
I would say clients still need a **person** when a payment is missing.
think: The **mortgage** and school costs already use most of our lower income.
Less than a month saved makes a **house repair** a real worry.
do: Keep preparing **client accounts** with Dalia’s review.
Transfer **ten weekly** from pay into a repair fund.
Bring **lunch from home** twice weekly to free that money.
feel: I feel **anxious** about ordinary household bills.
S0.quote: A broken washing machine would bother me more than a receipt sorter.
fieldNote: Her plateau anxiety comes from **household costs**, not from a prediction of job loss.
She uses AI **occasionally** for draft emails but keeps numeric and supervisory checks.

steps.text: Keep preparing client accounts under Dalia’s review
Transfer ten from weekly pay into household repair fund
Bring lunch from home twice weekly

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The drafted emails and return checks would change first. I can learn a tool, but I need the firm to tell me what happens to my hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that juniors need a real chance to learn why a return is wrong, not only a button that says finished. I would ask Dalia whether the firm will still fill the open junior seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think our routine files could be done by one person with software, and I expect my own hours to be cut. My partner Omar earns from driving a school bus, but his wage cannot carry the mortgage and both children alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take the firm’s paid supervised session on the approved review tool if Dalia offers it, then test it on old anonymised returns. If my paid hours fall in the first year, I would switch my daughter Nia from the paid dance class to the free community session and ask Omar to check for advertised evening bus-office shifts with stated pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because losing even one workday a week would upset the mortgage plan. I can learn, but I cannot make our bills wait for a course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask about the open seat?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A junior left last month, and nobody has posted the replacement. I would ask Dalia whether there is still a funded vacancy before telling anyone that we are safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Omar take more driving?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the bus company actually posts paid evening office hours that fit the children’s pickup. My partner Omar would take paid bus-office shifts only if the company offers hours around school pickup.

say: I would ask if the open **junior vacancy** is still funded.
I would insist juniors learn to spot **wrong returns**, not only press a button.
think: My **paid hours** could fall as routine files shrink.
Omar’s bus wage cannot cover the **mortgage and children** alone.
do: Take **paid supervised AI training** if Dalia offers it.
Move Nia to **free dance** if my hours fall.
Have Omar take **paid evening shifts** if my hours fall, shifts are offered, and school pickup fits.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely lost hours and mortgage pressure.
S1.quote: My partner Omar would take paid bus-office shifts only if the company offers hours around school pickup.
fieldNote: The unposted **junior replacement** makes her fear of reduced hours concrete.
Her backup income depends on **advertised paid shifts** that fit childcare, while her own learning requires supervision.

steps.text: Take paid supervised AI session if Dalia offers it
Move daughter Nia to free dance if hours fall
Have Omar take offered paid bus-office shifts if my hours fall and pickup fits

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two years would reach the next school fees before I could become a different kind of accountant. Robots later would not protect our screens.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say clients need a named person to answer when AGI prepares tax returns in 2028. I would also tell my family that hands-on robots around 2031 are a later change, so the accounting desk is first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the firm to drop the junior posts, including mine, when cheap thinking work arrives. Omar’s school bus wage and our tiny savings would not cover the mortgage for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask our lender what hardship help requires and transfer ten from each weekly pay into the repair fund as cash. If my accounting pay stops in the first year after 2028, I would apply for a posted school-office payroll role only if its stated wage covers our mortgage, seek a lender hardship pause if eligible, and ask my parents for a short grocery loan only if the lender cannot pause a payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed and keep thinking about the children’s rooms. I have calls to make, but no promise that any vacancy or lender help will come through.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my daughter Nia and son Felix that we are keeping the house plan simple and pausing paid activities. I would not tell my children a school-office job is waiting when nobody has advertised it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why that particular payroll role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know the school calendar from Omar’s work, and payroll has a human side I might learn. I would take a short local payroll class only if a free place fits pickup; a class by itself would not guarantee the vacancy.

say: I would ask who **answers clients** for 2028 tax returns.
I would say robots around **2031** are too late to shelter our desk work.
think: I expect my **junior post** to disappear when AGI reaches tax returns in 2028.
Omar’s bus wage and under-one-month **savings** cannot carry the mortgage.
do: Add **ten weekly** from pay to cash and take a free payroll class only if pickup fits.
Apply for **posted payroll work** if accounting pay stops after 2028 and wages cover the mortgage.
Ask **lender rules** now; after job loss seek a pause if eligible, then parents' grocery loan only if refused.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about the mortgage and children’s rooms.
S2.quote: I would not tell my children a school-office job is waiting when nobody has advertised it.
fieldNote: Her fallback to school payroll needs a **posted mortgage-covering wage**, not only a familiar setting.
Family help is a **last conditional step** after lender relief fails; the free class also depends on pickup hours.

steps.text: Transfer ten from weekly pay into cash repair buffer
Apply for posted school payroll job after 2028 accounting pay stops if wage covers mortgage
Ask lender pause rules now; seek eligible relief after loss; request parents' food loan if refused
Take free payroll class only if place fits pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me several school years to learn without leaving the children short of a wage. I would still want to see a real job at the end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell coworkers that the firm should show a paid route from junior tax work into payroll or client support. AGI reaches the accounts desk in 2031, and robots around 2034 will not give us three extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my return hours could be cut, but five years lets me practise payroll at school or the firm while Omar keeps driving. We could build a couple of months of savings if I put aside a small amount each payday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would enrol in the community college’s free evening payroll class if the place and pickup schedule are confirmed, and ask Dalia for one paid payroll case a month if the firm has one. I would move ten from each weekly pay into savings; in the first year after 2031 I would apply to posted payroll roles only if the salary covers the mortgage and childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but I can imagine finishing a class before my job changes. I would not spend the children’s food money on a course fee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would watch Felix during the class?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Omar could collect Felix on his usual bus route if the class starts after pickup. If the timetable clashes, I would wait for another free session rather than pay for evening care.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave the firm early?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a written payroll offer with enough pay and reliable hours. There are few similar accounting jobs nearby, so leaving my current pay for a possible post would be foolish.

say: I would seek a **paid route** from junior tax work into payroll.
I would name **2031** as the desk date, before robots around 2034.
think: A confirmed free class and small **weekly savings** give us some control.
do: Enrol in a **confirmed free payroll class** if pickup fits; practise a paid monthly case if Dalia offers one.
Save **ten from weekly pay** while I still earn.
Take only **written payroll offers** after 2031 with reliable hours and pay covering mortgage and childcare.
feel: I feel **anxious**, but able to study before the cut.
S3.quote: I would not spend the children’s food money on a course fee.
fieldNote: Her evening class depends on a **free place** and Omar’s existing school pickup route.
She ties any move to **written pay and hours**, which matters with few nearby accounting firms.

steps.text: Enrol in free payroll class if confirmed place fits pickup
Transfer ten weekly from pay into savings
Take posted payroll job after 2031 with reliable hours and written pay covering mortgage and childcare
Practise one paid payroll case monthly if Dalia offers a real case

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would bring Felix nearly through school. I could learn gradually and see whether the payroll idea stands up.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the firm has time to teach junior accountants real client and payroll work before AGI reaches the desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 are a later risk for hands-on jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect basic return fees to fall eventually, but I could have a payroll record and a larger cash cushion by 2036. I would not call my current junior wage safe forever just because the change is farther away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my current client files under Dalia’s review, take the free evening payroll class when a place fits pickup, and transfer ten from each weekly pay into savings. In the first year after 2036, if tax hours fall, I would take a posted payroll job only with a written wage covering the mortgage and family bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the mortgage even while the tax work continues. A decade lets me keep paying the loan while learning in steps.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you change the mortgage now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, Omar and I would keep the current payment and avoid a larger loan. We would revisit the house only if my wage actually stopped.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would help at the firm?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Dalia to let juniors practise on supervised payroll cases if the firm has them. If she offers paid time, I would attend and work through a real case with her. I learn more from fixing one real error than from watching a hundred quick demonstrations.

say: I would ask for **supervised payroll cases** before 2036.
I would say robots around **2039** do not protect accounting screens in 2036.
think: Basic return **fees** may fall, and my junior wage is not guaranteed.
A payroll record and **larger cushion** could grow over ten years.
do: Keep **client files** under Dalia’s review while learning.
Take the **free payroll class** if pickup fits; practise supervised cases on paid time if Dalia offers them.
Save **ten weekly**; take posted payroll work after 2036 hour cuts only with written wages covering mortgage and family bills.
feel: I feel **anxious** about today’s mortgage, though the longer warning helps.
S4.quote: I learn more from fixing one real error than from watching a hundred quick demonstrations.
fieldNote: Her long plan keeps **current pay** while she learns and deposits new weekly cash.
Any later payroll move depends on **posted wages** covering mortgage and family bills, not a title.

steps.text: Keep preparing client files under Dalia’s review
Take free payroll class if pickup fits; practise paid cases if Dalia offers
Transfer ten weekly from pay into savings
Take posted payroll job after 2036 hour cuts with written pay covering mortgage and bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my junior post and its wage could disappear before a payroll job opens. A real posted vacancy, a free class that fits school pickup, and lender hardship help if we qualify would help. I would ask family for food money only if the lender could not pause a payment.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who gets the children home while parents retrain. A free class is no use if I have to pay someone to collect my son Felix. A timetable is as important to me as the course fee.

headlineQuote: A free class is no use if I have to pay someone to collect my son Felix.
portrait: Bianca is a **43-year-old** junior accountant with a bachelor’s degree who prepares accounts under Dalia’s review.
She has **low pay**, under a month saved, a school-bus-driver partner, two children, and a mortgage.
She uses **AI occasionally** for checked draft emails and lives near few other accounting firms.
The **2028** shock threatens her junior wage; payroll work needs a posted salary covering household bills.
Longer warning allows **free evening study** if school pickup works and small new weekly deposits while employed.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her junior pay before a mortgage-covering payroll role appears.
whatWouldHelp: She wants a **posted vacancy**, free pickup-compatible training, and lender help if eligible.
